name: The Spirit in Redemption: Regeneration and Indwelling
path: Pneumatology: The Doctrine of the Holy Spirit

objectives.text: Identify the Holy Spirit as the One who gives new life to God's people
Name the Holy Spirit as the Helper Jesus promised would live with and in his followers
Retell Jesus' conversation with Nicodemus about being born again of the Spirit
Explain how Jesus' picture of the wind shows that the Spirit's work of new birth is real even though it cannot be seen
Describe from Jesus' words how the Spirit bears witness to Jesus and glorifies him
Explain regeneration as the Spirit's work of giving a new heart, using God's promise in Ezekiel
Explain what Scripture means when it says the Holy Spirit dwells in every believer
Describe the spiritual deadness of a person before regeneration and explain from Scripture why no one can cause their own new birth
Compare the person who is in the flesh with the person who is in the Spirit as Paul describes them in Romans 8
Explain how the Spirit's indwelling makes the believer's body a temple and identify what Paul says this means for how the body is used
Trace the Old Testament promises of the Spirit's coming to their fulfillment at Pentecost
Explain from Scripture how the Spirit uses the Word of God as the means of regeneration
Analyze how the Reformed confessions describe the Spirit as the One who unites believers to Christ
Explain the Spirit's role in applying to believers the redemption purchased by Christ
Explain effectual calling and why the Reformed tradition teaches that regeneration precedes and produces faith
Explain the Spirit's baptism of all believers into the one body of Christ
Interpret Paul's description of the indwelling Spirit as a seal and a guarantee of the believer's future inheritance
Analyze how Romans 8 links the Spirit's present indwelling to the future resurrection of the body
Distinguish regeneration from conversion, justification, and sanctification as the Reformed confessions define them
Defend from Scripture and the confessions the Reformed teaching that the Spirit's regenerating work is necessary for salvation
Compare the Reformed monergistic view of regeneration with synergistic and baptismal regeneration views
Evaluate the second blessing view of Spirit baptism against the view that every believer receives Spirit baptism at conversion
Explain the Westminster Confession's teaching on the regeneration of elect infants and others incapable of being outwardly called by the Word
Compose a theological essay that synthesizes regeneration and indwelling within the Spirit's application of Christ's redemption

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (new life, Helper, born of the Spirit, indwelling, flesh and Spirit, temple, union with Christ, applying redemption, effectual calling, Spirit baptism, second blessing, necessity of regeneration). Merged the duplicate grade 8 and grade 12 application of redemption objectives and recast grade 12 as a create task. Dropped the indwelling and assurance objective since assurance belongs to the sibling sub-topic, and removed Heidelberg Q1 for the same reason. Added Nicodemus retelling, wind image, Ezekiel new heart promise, spiritual deadness, Pentecost fulfillment, the Word as means of regeneration, sealing, indwelling and resurrection, distinguishing regeneration from related doctrines, comparison with synergistic and baptismal regeneration views, and WCF 10.3 on elect infants. Replaced vague verbs (observe, apply the truth) with observable ones and added verse-level anchors and confession references that state each doctrine.
